newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Village sees higher year profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Village sees higher year profit.

text.p: Entertainment group Village Roadshow Ltd said on Tuesday it expected its profit for the year to June 1997 to be comfortably ahead of last year.
"This year we are forecasting a profit comfortably ahead of last year," chairman Robert Kirby told the annual meeting.
"Certainly over the next two years, we expect profits to continue to grow despite the inevitable pressures of our broad and international investment programme," he said.
Village Roadshow reported a net profit of A$47.49 million in the 1995/96 year, up from A$38.00 million a year earlier on sales of A$297.12 million, up from A$246.62 million.
Kirby said that over the next two to three years, the company would be recreating itself as a world force in cinema while continuing to manage the real expansion opportunities in all its businesses.
"All this expansion will take Village Roadshow to a higher plain ... our next big leap in growth," he said.

"This period of the next 18 to 24 months can be parallelled with, or seen as a replay of, the broad investment in our future five years ago leading up to the launch of Movie World and multiplexing in Australia," he said.
Kirby said three separate research studies had placed Village Roadshow ahead of any other company in Australia in shareholder return and increased value over the past five years.
He noted the company raised A$215 million of new equity during the latest financial year.
"The strength of our balance sheet is fundamental to our ability to envisage, plan and create the businesses of Village Roadshow into the first decade of the next century," he said.
Funds were used to help buy 50 percent of the Warner Bros cinemas in the UK and Germany.
Warner Bros is part of Time Warner Inc.
"The full potential and value to our group of this deal is not yet perceived by the market," Kirby said.

"In long term strategic terms, this is the step to the altar, the marriage of the interests of Warner Bros and Village Roadshow that have been engaged and blossoming over the past 25 years...from production, distribution, theme parks, and Warner Stores to, now, cinema exhibition across the globe from Argentina to Europe, Taiwan and Australia," he said.
The aim was to become the world's biggest cinema exhibitor.

Warner has 143 screens at 16 sites in UK with 16 sites under construction and seven more committed. "We plan to dramatically accelerate the growth there and expect to have 45 sites with 551 screens within the next five years making ours the largest cinema circuit in England, helped by the megaplexes of 15 - 30 screens we will be building," Kirby said.

In Germany, there are 26 screens at three sites with many more in the pipeline. "As with England, we have a unique opportunity to become the number one exhibitor in Germany, forecasting to grow to 522 screens at 64 sites by 2001."
